about.title: Newman Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Newman is a small place — just under 11,000 people in western Stanislaus County — and when a family here loses someone suddenly, the whole town tends to feel it. Public records show no traffic deaths inside city limits in 2025, with seven injury collisions reported that year, most often clustering on Thursday afternoons. Those figures offer little comfort to a household whose loss traced back to a crash on Inyo Avenue or N Street, a fall at a worksite, a faulty product, or a medical error that should not have happened. A wrongful death claim is the civil process California gives surviving relatives to recover what a death actually costs them: funeral and burial expenses, the income and support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of their love, companionship and guidance. It moves on its own track, apart from any criminal case. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Newman families with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What a Newman Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not everyone can bring the claim
items.desc: California gives first standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children; certain dependents and heirs may qualify only when those relatives are absent. Sorting out who files, and in what order, is one of the first things an attorney will help you settle.

items.title: The clock is shorter than it feels
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death. If a city, county or other government entity may share fault, the window to give notice is considerably shorter, so waiting to ask is the riskiest choice.

items.title: A civil claim stands on its own
items.desc: Whether or not a prosecutor brings charges, your family's civil case proceeds separately and does not depend on a conviction. It is the avenue for recovering funeral costs, lost support, and the loss of companionship and guidance.

items.question: Newman reported zero traffic deaths in 2025 — does that mean wrongful death claims don't happen here?
items.answer: No. The 2025 record covers roadway deaths inside city limits, but families in Newman also lose loved ones to crashes on nearby highways, agricultural and industrial accidents, medical mistakes, and unsafe products. Each of those can support a wrongful death claim if someone else's negligence played a role. The low local count simply reflects one year of one category of loss.

items.question: Who is actually allowed to file a wrongful death lawsuit in California?
items.answer: The law gives priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. When there is no spouse, partner or child, certain financially dependent relatives or legal heirs may be able to file instead. Because the rules are specific, an attorney will confirm your standing before anything is filed.

items.question: How long do we have, and does it change if a government agency was involved?
items.answer: Generally, a wrongful death lawsuit must be filed within two years of the date of death. If the responsible party might be a public entity — for example, a city or county vehicle or a poorly maintained public road — you must submit a formal claim on a much shorter timeline before a lawsuit can proceed. It's wise to speak with an attorney well before either deadline approaches.
